resource.name: PM Horoscope
resource.description: Daily reading based on twelve corpus-derived PM archetypes. Deterministic, no LLM call.

tools.name: pm_horoscope_read
tools.description: Returns today's PM horoscope reading for a chosen archetype. Deterministic, composed from date + archetype.

archetype.description: User's archetype, set once via quiz or direct pick.

date.description: ISO date. Defaults to today if omitted.

tools.name: pm_horoscope_quiz
tools.description: Returns the six-question archetype quiz. User answers map to one of twelve archetypes.

answers.description: Six integer answers, indices into each question's options.

next_archetype.description: Second-closest archetype, in case the user disagrees with the primary.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.comment: MCP resource spec for #53 PM Horoscope. Phase 2 .mcpb bundle target. Validated against MCP Apps spec (Jan 2026 release + current draft) on 2026-05-18.
dev.workingfromlenny.open_questions: Confirm `mimeType: text/html` is the right way to declare UI resource vs structured output.
Decide whether quiz state lives in the server (persistent across sessions) or in the host (cookie/local-storage).
dev.workingfromlenny.proposed_answers: mimeType: text/html is correct for embedded UI resources rendered as cards in the host. The MCP Apps spec uses `text/html;profile=mcp-app` as the canonical MIME for UI bundles; clients negotiate this in their `mimeTypes` capability. The bare `text/html` here is the user-facing rendering hint at the resource level; the actual bundle payload should advertise the full `text/html;profile=mcp-app` profile when served.

Split by context. Web version: host-side (cookie or localStorage) for the chosen archetype. No server needed for a one-time selection, and the web version has no backend. MCP version: server data-dir under the bundle's own scope. There is no manifest-level consent flag — if the MCP version stores the archetype, surface it in the tool's description so the host's confirmation UI conveys the persistence to the user.

notes: ui:// scheme is valid; no rigid format is enforced — server-defined slugs after the scheme are acceptable.

No requires-consent / data-retention / fs-write capability exists in either ext-apps appCapabilities or .mcpb manifest. Consent is host-discretion; readOnlyHint: false on stateful tools is the only normative hook.
Canonical UI-bundle MIME is text/html;profile=mcp-app per the spec's mimeTypes negotiation.
Underscore-prefixed fields at non-_meta paths have undefined host behavior; project metadata lives under _meta with reverse-DNS keys.
